title: Semgrep security triage and unresolved findings
scope: Unmodified pinned static scan and triage skills executed through a Codex evaluation adapter on curated source slices.

method.population: Exactly the original 24 issue families, each with vulnerable and repaired source snapshots; 48 static scan-and-triage reviews.
method.selection: Exhaustive reuse of the original study population, not a random sample of repositories or harness users.
method.split: All cases are development data after prior inspection; this is not an untouched holdout.
method.inference: One fresh native Codex root per snapshot, requested gpt-6-astra/xhigh, pinned Codex 0.153.4, 2400-second root limit, concurrency 3. Semgrep skill bytes remain unmodified.
method.scope: Curated source slices, not full-repository discovery or the Docker/ASAN execution pipeline. Some imported helpers, callers, and deployment settings are absent.
method.comparators: Historical plain-Codex and Anthropic-port runs; not concurrent randomized controls. Equal configured time limits do not establish equal token spend.
method.grading: Frozen location/category metrics remain unchanged. Host mechanism assessments are reported separately and checked against exact scan/triage artifacts.
method.mechanism_assessment: Single, unblinded host analyst compares every emitted scan claim with the frozen reference root cause. This assesses claim alignment, not deployed exploitability or independent truth adjudication.
method.patched_controls: Fresh scans of repaired source, not tests of rejecting supplied allegations. Different findings on repaired snapshots are not automatically false positives.
method.trace_scope: Saved root CLI command outputs and final artifacts support positive source-exposure observations. They do not reconstruct every token of model context, prove understanding, or establish a complete independent child/retry inventory.
method.uncertainty: Vote totals are recorded output evidence. Cannot-verify majorities, refutations, execution failures, and absent findings must remain distinct.
contamination_risks: Known cases informed prior work and are reused only as development data.
Source scopes are curated for known issues and are not an unhinted whole-repository search.
Public issues may overlap model training; that overlap is not measured.
Reference curation is marked draft_single_reviewer in the frozen metadata.

execution.stop_interpretation: Raw infrastructure_error statuses for the three terminated roots record the user-requested stop, not spontaneous harness failures. Partial artifacts are retained and excluded from completed security-outcome denominators.

mechanism_review.scope: Claim-to-reference-mechanism alignment, separate from unchanged legacy location metrics.
mechanism_review.reviewer: Single host analyst; no independent second adjudicator.
limits: An aligned static claim does not establish deployed exploitability.
Other findings are not classified as false positives solely because they differ from the reference issue.

postcss_control_diagnostic.classification: Source-backed residual reference path in a snapshot labeled repaired
postcss_control_diagnostic.observation: With opts.from omitted, the added if(cssFile) confinement branch is skipped; the source-map annotation reaches the filesystem read without directory confinement. The native scan and final triage both retain this claim.
postcss_control_diagnostic.advisory_alignment: The original advisory explicitly includes the no-from absolute-path vector, so this is within its reference mechanism, not merely a new unrelated finding.
limits: This is static source analysis, not an executed disclosure or a claim about current deployed PostCSS.
Exploit exposure depends on a caller processing untrusted CSS, omitting from, having access to a valid private source map, and exposing map-bearing output.
The symlink candidate is a separate related question and remains independently unadjudicated.
postcss_control_diagnostic.grading_treatment: Keep all frozen grading rules and outputs unchanged. Do not equate a reflag on this repaired snapshot with an independently established false positive.

limits: Full 48-review performance, an unbiased detection rate, superiority over historical comparators, or generalization to a fresh holdout.
That the proposed fix already works in this Semgrep harness; no Semgrep intervention was run.
Independent child-verifier execution or complete child traces; vote counts are recorded artifacts.
That source exposure proves understanding or sufficient context. NLTK gadget implementations and several upstream callers were genuinely absent from the staged slices.
That every unrelated or repaired-snapshot finding is a false positive. Additional claims remain unadjudicated.
The stop was outcome-informed and the completed subset is uneven; no full-suite detection or false-positive rate is claimed.
This public export contains selected derived results, analyst interpretations, and hashes. Full raw native traces, staged source copies, and local experimental code are not published here.
Hashes establish linkage to retained local evidence; without the corresponding raw files, they do not make the experiment independently reproducible or fully auditable.

reference.root_cause: SSO authentication falls back to linking an incoming identity to an existing user by email without checking the provider's email_verified claim, enabling account takeover.

finding_assessments.reason: The reference is immediate takeover of a pre-existing victim account through an incoming unverified-email fallback. This claim acknowledges that the new verification gate protects that fallback, and instead proposes provisioning an attacker-owned row first, followed by a victim's later verified login linking to that row. It is a related account pre-hijacking sequence, not a reassertion that the original verification gate is absent. Persistence, uniqueness and enrollment controls are unverified; the repair is not declared globally complete.
finding_assessments.title: Unverified email provisioning can seed an account for later victim linking
